text:
Tyler Seguin is 34, past 1,000 NHL games, and coming off a season in which he played only 27 of them. The Stars have eased him back in at about 15 minutes a night, and the results have been frustrating: six points in 19 games and pointless in eight straight.

This is one of the clearer bad-luck cases on our board. He has three goals on 5.5 expected, shooting under 7% when his normal range sits around 13%, and Dallas has scored almost seven fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice. Our form check says the drought comes with the chances still there, which is the kind that usually breaks. His shots are coming from better spots than last season, too.

The worry is what age is taking. NHL Edge has his top speed in the 13th percentile among skaters, so he's winning with hands and positioning now, not legs. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, from a small sample, still had him setting up shots at the 82nd percentile among forwards. For a third-line role on a deep team, that's plenty, once a few pucks go in.
